trigger_event: U.S. Defense Logistics Agency announces $300M strategic lithium‑carbonate contract targeting non‑Chinese sources
market_equilibrium_shift: Transition from a China‑centric lithium supply chain to a diversified, security‑driven non‑Chinese strategic stockpile equilibrium

opportunities.title: Award of the $300M DLA lithium‑carbonate contract to a Zimbabwean consortium
required_missing_nodes: non‑Chinese supplier node linked to DLA
opportunities.justification: The DLA lacks a non‑Chinese supplier capable of delivering battery‑grade lithium carbonate under a fixed‑price, multi‑year contract.

opportunities.title: Construction/upgrade of a battery‑grade lithium carbonate refinery in Zimbabwe
required_missing_nodes: domestic processing facility node (lithium carbonate refinery)
financing & risk‑mitigation instrument edges (Export‑Import Bank, ADB guarantees)
regulatory alignment edge to U.S. DoD/EPA standards

capital_flow.likely_funder: U.S. Defense Production Act financing, private equity, EU technology partners

opportunities.justification: Current supply chain lacks a processing node that can convert concentrate to battery‑grade carbonate meeting U.S. defense specifications.

opportunities.title: Establishment of a U.S.–Zimbabwe strategic lithium stockpile hub
required_missing_nodes: stockpile storage facility node in Zimbabwe
continuous financing edge for inventory management

capital_flow.beneficiary: Strategic stockpile hub operator (U.S. Army Materiel Command partner)
capital_flow.likely_funder: U.S. DLA procurement budget and ancillary logistics service contracts

opportunities.justification: The graph lacks a secure, compliant logistics and storage link connecting the DLA to a non‑Chinese lithium carbonate source.

pipeline_metadata.core_event: The U.S. Defense Logistics Agency issued a $300 million contract to secure lithium supplies, a move that could boost Zimbabwe’s lithium production and processing as the United States seeks to reduce reliance on China.
